solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Good fellow in row G has argument

indicators.note: in places the good-fellow pair inside the row word plus the letter from the clue, before its end

parts.note: a din is a noisy row, a racket
a don is a fellow of a college at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A decent chap sitting in row G of a theatre gets into a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' tempts as the argument, but here it means din. The definition is 'argument', with 'has' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ding-dong is informal British for a heated quarrel or noisy set-to.

clue.text: Mob having leader supplanted by Dutch tinker

indicators.note: the first letter of the mob word is swapped out for the Dutch abbreviation

parts.note: a rabble is a disorderly mob

explanation.surface: A crowd whose ringleader is replaced by a Dutchman who fiddles about.
explanation.definitionFit: To tinker with something is to dabble in it, meddling without serious skill.

clue.text: Unofficial titles such as clink and choky

definitions.meaning: informal names given in place of real ones
clink and choky are slang names for 'nick', British slang for prison

explanation.surface: Informal names, for instance 'clink' and 'choky'.
explanation.walkthrough: Clink, choky and nick are all British slang for prison, so these words are literally names for the nick.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicknames are familiar substitute names, unofficial labels rather than formal titles.

clue.text: Females securing second jabs

indicators.note: the females' word holds the abbreviation for second inside it

parts.note: does are female deer or rabbits

explanation.surface: Women getting their second vaccinations booked.
explanation.definitionFit: Jabs are informal for injections, and each vaccine injection is a dose.

clue.text: Most elegant swallow occupies shelter

indicators.note: the swallowing word takes up residence inside the shelter word

parts.note: a nest is a bird's shelter
to swallow food is to eat it

explanation.surface: The smartest swallow has moved into a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' reads as the bird, matching the shelter, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatest is the superlative of neat, meaning trim, tidy and elegant.

clue.text: Collection initially is feted as "top of the range"

parts.note: a mass is a large collection of things

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of the two following words

explanation.surface: A collection is praised as the very best of a product line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top of the range' reads as marketing praise, but a range here is a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains, the high mass forming the summit area of a range.

clue.text: Hit that must have come from Sky

definitions.text: Hit that must have come from Sky

parts.words: Hit that must have come from Sky
parts.note: reads like a hit TV show from the broadcaster Sky, but describes a military attack from the air

explanation.surface: A smash-hit programme that surely originated on Sky television.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster, so 'Hit' first suggests a popular show.
explanation.definitionFit: An attack by aircraft on a target is a blow delivered literally out of the sky.

clue.text: Kept bringing up Hindu gods

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing something up reads it from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: devas are gods or divine beings in Hinduism

explanation.surface: Someone held on to the Hindu deities while raising them.
explanation.definitionFit: Saved and kept are synonyms in the sense of retained or put aside.

clue.text: Spooner's tipsy enthusiast is steerer of boat

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: merry is mildly drunk
a fan is an enthusiast

explanation.surface: A slightly drunk devotee who is also the one steering a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferryman operates a ferry, piloting the boat across the water.

clue.text: Onboard expert with a verdict: brake's worn

indicators.note: worn suggests the letters have been battered out of their shape and reworked

explanation.surface: A mechanic's judgement on a car: its brakes are worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn' rearranges A VERDICT BRAKES. 'Onboard expert' is ironic: a passenger who keeps telling the driver what to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A backseat driver is a passenger offering unwanted advice, a self-appointed expert on board the car.

clue.text: See 9
Letter for radio penned by Czechoslovakian

indicators.note: penned by says the answer is enclosed within the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A letter for broadcast written by someone from Czechoslovakia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' suggests correspondence, but it is a single letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Echo is the NATO phonetic alphabet's word for E, used in radio communication.

clue.text: Chuck cycling for fish

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter from one end of the word round to the other

parts.note: to sling is to chuck or throw

explanation.surface: Someone named Chuck goes cycling to catch fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the S of SLING from front to back.
explanation.definitionFit: Lings are long slender food fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Old quote Dolly regularly used with enthusiasm

parts.note: ex- means former, old
to cite is to quote

indicators.note: regularly picks alternate letters from the name, first third and fifth

explanation.surface: An old quotation from Dolly, used often and keenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Excitedly describes acting eagerly and animatedly, full of enthusiasm.

clue.text: Charm smuggler into bath when naked

indicators.note: into puts the smuggler word inside what remains of the bath
naked means stripped of outer covering, so the bath loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a mule is a person who smuggles drugs

explanation.surface: A drug runner slips into the bath without any clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when naked' strips BATH to AT.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is an ornament worn as a charm against evil or bad luck.

clue.text: Celebrated finale below stage (area really empty)

indicators.note: in a down clue below places the finale word under the stage word

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
the end is the finale

indicators.note: empty removes the inside of the word, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A famous final act below the stage, with the space truly vacant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' suggests a theatre, but it is a leg of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Legendary means very famous, the stuff of legend.

clue.text: Home and Away briefly set on fine island

indicators.note: in an across answer, set on puts the home-and-away letters after the fine word

parts.note: OK means fine
in means at home

indicators.note: briefly cuts the last letter off the word

explanation.surface: A soap opera, Home and Away, briefly filmed on a beautiful island.
explanation.walkthrough: Home and Away is an Australian TV soap, popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Okinawa is the main island of Japan's Ryukyu chain.

clue.text: Bother adorning most of tomb with marble

indicators.note: adorning puts the shortened tomb word into the marble word as decoration

parts.note: agate is a banded stone, and an agate is also a kind of playing marble

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter

parts.note: a grave is a tomb

explanation.surface: Fussing over decorating nearly all of a tomb with marble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims GRAVE to GRAV.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggravate is informally to annoy or irritate, to bother someone.

clue.text: Pay out when organising bus rides

indicators.note: organising means putting the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Spending money on arranging bus trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organising' rearranges BUS RIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: To disburse is to pay out money from a fund.

clue.text: Perception of thing is shifting

indicators.note: shifting means moving the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: How a thing is perceived keeps changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' rearranges THING IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is perceptive understanding, the ability to see into a matter.

clue.text: Draws Cram running toward the north

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to swot is British slang for studying hard, cramming

explanation.surface: Steve Cram running northwards draws level.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Cram is a British middle-distance runner, so 'running' fits the athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: To tow is to draw or pull along behind.

clue.text: Vehicle butcher reported

indicators.note: reported signals a word that sounds the same as the butchering word

parts.note: to butcher is to slaughter, slay

explanation.surface: A vehicle belonging to a butcher, according to news reports.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh is a sledge drawn by horses or reindeer, a vehicle for snow.

clue.text: Batch of beers let go, saving nine pence

indicators.note: saving means keeping inside, so the sacking word holds the others

parts.note: to sack someone is to let them go from a job
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Fired employee spends on beer but still saves ninepence.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-pack is a pack of six cans or bottles, a batch of beers.

clue.text: Advice for 9, 10's own safety

parts.note: tells the backseat driver to buckle a seatbelt for safety, and also, in slang, to shut up

explanation.surface: A tip offered for a backseat driver's own protection.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is both 'fasten your seatbelt' and British slang for 'be quiet', exactly what a backseat driver needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Belt up means fasten one's seatbelt, and is also a curt order to stop talking.

clue.text: Brazilian stripping for the beach?

parts.note: a Brazilian is a style of hair removal, stripping hair to prepare for swimwear

explanation.surface: A Brazilian person undressing to go to the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brazilian' reads as a person from Brazil, but is a type of waxing.
explanation.definitionFit: This hair-removal treatment clears the area a swimsuit leaves exposed, and a Brazilian is one form of it.

clue.text: Drunken doctor admits fighting with sticks

indicators.note: admits means the phrase lets the answer in, holding it within its letters

explanation.surface: An inebriated medic confesses to brawling with sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendo is the Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords.

clue.text: Waffle dish changing hands

indicators.note: changing hands swaps L for left into R for right

parts.note: a plate is a dish

explanation.surface: A plate of waffles gets passed to someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waffle' looks like a breakfast food next to 'dish', but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To prate is to talk foolishly at length, to waffle.

clue.text: Bird missing kernel of slim nut

indicators.note: missing means the bird lacks the letters taken from slim

parts.note: a pelican is a large water bird

indicators.note: kernel means the core, the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A bird that has missed out on the kernel of a slender nut.
explanation.walkthrough: The kernel of SLIM is LI.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is the edible nut of a North American hickory tree.

clue.text: One in flight essentially leaving taxi here

indicators.note: essentially points at the very centre of the word, and leaving removes that letter

parts.note: a runaway is someone fleeing, in flight

explanation.surface: A fugitive basically leaving by taxi from here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' and 'taxi' both suggest air travel and escape; the A at the centre of RUNAWAY is dropped. 'taxi here' is a place where planes taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft taxi along a runway before take-off and after landing.

clue.text: Pub talk about brewer's last diagram

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: about means the talk word goes round the brewer's final letter

parts.note: to chat is to talk

indicators.note: last takes the final letter of the brewer word

explanation.surface: Pub conversation about the latest from a brewery's diagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar chart is a diagram showing quantities as bars of different lengths.

clue.text: Name juvenile in centre of demo

indicators.note: in places the juvenile word inside the central letters of demo
centre takes the middle letters of the word

parts.note: a pony is a small horse, the mount for a youngster, taken loosely here as a young one

explanation.surface: A young person named at the heart of a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of DEMO is EM.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym is a name derived from a person, or the person a thing is named after.

clue.text: Shallow end pike's ravaged

indicators.note: ravaged means wrecked, so the letters are torn up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: In the shallow end, a pike has been savaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shallow end' reads as part of a pool, but 'end' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin-deep means superficial, going no deeper than the surface, so shallow.
